reviews.text: This review doesn't show the 100+ hours I have on the demos and playtests. This is a gem of a game. It has its own idea that feels so good, mixing positioning and deckbuilding, but it's all about synergies. The cool thing is that it's extremely simple to understand initially but hides a good amount of depth. The artstyle is quite dynamic and lively. So many little creatures, plants and more to discover. 8 mayors with different starters that play very differently and a huge pool of cute stuff to experiment with. And even several difficulties like you'd find in games like Slay the Spire for those who want extra challenge. For this price it's a steal. We could find some points that could be better, like how it could have more musics and maybe some other small details here and there. But nothing that would make me even remotely close to not recommending Wild City. (Played it on Steam Deck if anyone's interested. I usually play with left trackpad as mouse and the 2 triggers as L/R clicks. Feels very natural to me)

Not the greatest game of all time. But at such a cheap price its well worth it. That is to say its good enough. The characters/classes arent particularly interesting. They dont have any unique passives, or many exclusive cards, the only difference is their starting deck. Worse yet, alot of the cards that properly synergize with their starting decks seems to be unlocked by winning as the respective character. This is common for roguelikes. Some might say "oh but you need to beat the game as ironclad before unlocking his best block synergy cards, in slay the spire 2". But this is more extreme than that. Imagine instead that you unlock the silent in slay the spire 2: But instead; you only get 1 shiv card in your starting deck, 3 shiv card you MIGHT get from the shop, and the other 6 cards that make shiv work, you dont get until you beat the game. The rest of your deck is the same ironclad cards you have already used. Youre largely encouraged to remove all your unique cards, and make a generic deck instead. As everything that makes your character unique, is likely to be a hinderance until you win with the character. Thats alot. Im probably only upset because; different characters is my favorite part of rogue like deck builders. Another thing: the game is weirdly unoptimized. In game its not particularly noticeable. But Its CHUGGING during almost any loading screen. Like i have seen far more complex games, perform far better.

I've been loving the game since the demo and have been waiting for the full game to drop IMPATIENTLY. I would have paid twice, but I was VERY pleasantly surprised when I saw the price tag. It was a no-brainer for me to begin with, but less then a tenner, I was sold multiple times over. There are some minor hiccups, still - namely, it still shows "wishlist now" at the end of every game, and the loading screen causing a screeching halt. But the game as a whole is pure, ordered chaotic joy. And I cannot recommend it enough! Anyone enjoying a bit of chaotic engine building (think Wingspan but less order), this is the game for you. Everyone else, give it a shot - it's less then 10 BUCKS!

Honestly pretty amazing despite a few issues. The run structure, the cross-synergies, the way you draw and position, all while striking a good balance with the complexity of mechanics and is very intuitive for the most part. Dare I say the gameplay loop is easily among the best in the genre. The visuals are incredible as well. As for what I have a problem with, I think the stickers could have a few more unique effects and also need a bit of balancing as some are just universally better than others. I think the characters are [i]just[/i] different enough with their starter decks as it provides starting points for build directions, but unique passives would definitely make them perfect. The most egregious (and easily fixable part) are the unlocks. The amount of times you have to win with each character is absurd. The card pool feels a lot better the more of these you get, but you'll be spending a lot of time just to get to that point. Not to mention that the re-election difficulty (basically ascension) has 14 levels, and it's PER CHARACTER. While annoying, that doesn't take much away from how fun it is at its core. Outside of that and some technical hiccups during loading and lack of graphical options (and controller support if that's often what you use), it's still an easy recommend.

I enjoyed this game because the game design is welcoming. I'm not a big fan of deckbuilders because most of them require you to invest some time and effort to start having fun. It took me around 30 minutes to start enjoying this one while Inscription and Slay the Spire had me learning for more than 2 hours just to start having fun. I only have around two hours a week to play games, so being welcoming is a big plus for me.

The gameplay really clicks once the combos start rolling, turning each run into something satisfying, addictive, and fun to optimize. The synergy design gives you plenty of room to experiment without locking you into one path, while the art direction gives the game a lot of charm and personality. Came for the combos, stayed for the animal capitalism.

The art is amazing, going for a cartoony thick outline bobblehead style that pairs really well with the creative ways all these species are depicted and how their in-game effects tie into it. And there are so many, you may even learn something new from it! It truly makes the world of the game feel big. Its downsides are its rather lacking presentation outside the actual "cards", as well as the fact that mayors don't seem to differ in any way other than starting decks. Considering that, I would say it's just a tad expensive for what it offers, so maybe get it on a sale of some kind, but it's gameplay wise it will offer you pleeeenty of hours of enjoyment guaranteed, so even full price is probably worth it for many players, I would say.

[quote][h1]动物版幸运房东[/h1][/quote] 这是款类幸运房东，不断摆棋子计分的游戏 幸运房东玩法的本质是 玩家面对日益不够用的棋盘格子，想办法消除低分棋子，提高棋子的均分。 但是官方好像没理解此类游戏玩法设计本质与玩家通关的诀窍。 粗暴的加了一堆有看似想法的设计，但因为设计的词条逻辑实在太多，导致棋子间关联性不足。 且游戏玩家拒绝拿棋子与廉价刷新挑选棋子的机会。 这让游戏变得非常困难。看来一眼游戏成就，过关率不到五成。 游戏有着优秀的美术音乐，但是难度极大，运气成分极高。 故只推荐喜欢挑战难度大，且不介意运气因素的玩家。 [code] No Responsibility Review，只根据个人喜好进行评测： [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/36266776-NRR233] 无责任评测[/url][/code]

___一款类幸运房东游戏，内容量大管饱，流派多样性我认为远超猫神牧场（流派多样到像出了4、5个DLC或者更多目前我只解锁到第三个角色），有种以撒的爽感，而且还有不同的boss，数量固定，像杀戮尖塔经过一定的路线后打不同的boss（每局共三个）。 ___整体难度不是很难，注意选对动物（打完一些特定局可以选栖息地，选择对应栖息地动物种类达到数量后，可以将获得的分数翻倍），因为分数可以翻倍每个流派（目前倒计时流派最轮椅）几乎都可以玩，也有人说难度过高，实际我认为是太少人关注导致教程缺失、决策失误，在demo时我就开始玩蛮久了所以正式版对我而言不是很难。 ___比如有一个大王花每回合可以在周围六格召唤卡组中的一个无脊椎动物，升级后可以召唤两个，然后可以选择一些喜欢吃无脊椎动物的卡牌，也可以要一个建筑（比如育婴室可以让生成的卡牌消失，卡牌能获得它原本的分数而且消失后育婴室还能获得一些分数，当然你也可以放一只升级蟑螂，倒计时1回合{如果它相邻建筑那就在建筑周围生成2只蟑螂，当然会被育婴室回收这样就有无限位置可以生成蟑螂涮分}）。 ___还有一些小问题，有些时候右键没法看卡片详情，如果要SL只能退出游戏重新进，新手教程对游戏区块，标签，栖息地，建筑的定义没有明确告知，贴纸给人凑数的感觉，基本上区块相关的太弱了。 ___总而言之瑕不掩瑜，十分推荐！

[h2]Linear, Repetitive & Stale[/h2] While I did in fact enjoy the hexegonal strategy, once the first run was over, I realized exactly what the game was. It was an unrewarding time sink, where if you don't succeed on your first run, you get nothing. No new units, no new mayors, no new content, just a slap on the wrist followed by a "Do better next time, for a new mayor." Each path is the same, each run, unless you choose a different bracket of elements, even then being forced to choose a new card after every encounter, quickly bloats your deck, so you aim towards a beetle 200% luck or beetle $100 build to counter the default cards and stack up legendaries and specific structures that have great synergy, even then, unlocking anyone after Micha, is just... It's just such a damn chore, I played for 5 hours (steam offline mode doesn't count) and outside of just never finding a good deck or fun deck, the royalty free music and lack of atmosphere, just slowly drove me insane. [h2]Conclusion[/h2] It wasn't really all that fun. It lacked depth and replay value that rewarded success.
